title: About CAPIT | Data, Methodology, and Mission
description: Who runs CAPIT, how the well-plugging data works, what the token represents, what CAPIT does not claim, and letters from both founders.
headline: About CAPIT
body: CAPIT is a public data site owned and operated by Tellus Digital, LLC. Our mission is to make U.S. well-plugging progress easy to see and check: state records in one place, each with its source attached, free for anyone to use.

sections.heading: Why This Exists
sections.body: The United States has millions of abandoned oil and gas wells. EPA's greenhouse gas inventory estimates about 3.7 million, more than half of them unplugged. State inventories list roughly 142,000 documented orphan wells with no responsible operator, and hundreds of thousands more may be undocumented. The records that show progress are scattered across dozens of state systems, each with its own definitions and update schedule. CAPIT brings those records into one public view so anyone can see what is being counted, where it came from, and when it was last checked.

sections.heading: How CAPIT Works
sections.body: Every record moves through the same five steps, in order:
bullets: **Collect:** We gather public records from state oil and gas regulators and other approved public datasets.
**Normalize:** We map each state's fields into one schema and remove duplicates, so records can be compared across states.
**Verify:** We confirm each record exists at its source, shows a plugged status, and meets our publication rules. We do not inspect wells in the field.
**Publish:** Each record appears with its source, retrieval date, and any caveats.
**Link:** Each unique published record corresponds to one CAPIT token minted on Base. This is a rule about how token supply grows. It is not a claim on the well.

sections.heading: What CAPIT Is Not
sections.body: CAPIT is not a government registry and does not replace the official agency record. It does not plug wells or inspect plugging work. The registry and the token are separate things. The data is free to everyone, no wallet required, and holding CAPIT gives no claim on any well, any environmental benefit, or any public funds. The CAPIT token is a community token with meme characteristics: its price is driven by attention and demand, not by the wells in the registry. It is not a carbon credit, not an emissions offset, and not backed by any asset.

sections.heading: The People Behind CAPIT
sections.body: CAPIT is a two-person project of Tellus Digital, LLC. We think you should know who is making the judgment calls behind a public data set, so both of us have written openly about why we are doing this. Both letters are on the [Open Letters](/open-letter) page.

sections.heading: Steve Hillmer, Co-founder
sections.body:
CAPIT began as Steve's idea: that the record of America's well-plugging work exists, is public, and is almost impossible for an ordinary person to see. He leads partnerships and is the contact for sponsors, data providers, and state agencies.

[Read Steve's letter](/open-letter)

sections.heading: Alana Oldham, Co-founder, CEO, and Developer
sections.body:
Alana builds and runs the CAPIT platform: the data pipeline, the registry, the site, and the on-chain components. She is responsible for the publication rules and for keeping the registry open. The code is published for inspection at [github.com/alanaoldham-eng/capit](https://github.com/alanaoldham-eng/capit), so anyone can audit what the site and the pipeline actually do.

[Read Alana's letter](/open-letter)

sections.heading: Governance and Roadmap
sections.body: Tellus Digital, LLC owns CAPIT and operates the website, data pipeline, and minting process. The token contract's roles and permissions, including which addresses can mint, are visible on the verified contract on BaseScan. Roadmap updates will be posted here as they are approved. Our founder's [open letter](/open-letter) sets out the principles behind the project, the commitments we expect to be held to, and why we are seeking grant funding rather than building a paywall.
